propositions: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host's snapshot store remains append-only and never reclaims entries, causing unbounded disk growth on non-review-bot hosts

The GC trigger must follow the compact_trigger pattern: an O(1) in-process stamp check on gate-resolution tail with zero ticket-store lock, and heavy GC work offloaded to a detached child process outside hot paths

A detached child spawned on due cadence runs janitor.run_gc under snapshot-store-rooted gc/worker.lock and gc/flock sidecars, with single-flight adjudication and harmless overlap with the review-bot's resident janitor
The trigger is operation-linked and in-process, requiring no CI provider, cron, or daemon, and is disabled by setting interval_seconds <= 0
All worktrees on a host share one snapshot store and one GC clock/lock, keyed on the canonical store root per-host
